---
title: "stateMINT: the emulator"
---

`stateMINT` takes the EIR at the point a campaign is deployed, the setting it belongs to, and the
campaign under evaluation, and returns prevalence and clinical-case trajectories over six years,
three before the campaign and three after. The EIR comes from
[estiMINT](../04-estimint/index.qmd). The *state* in the name is the state-space architecture, a
Mamba2 layer carrying a hidden vector along the sequence, and not an epidemiological compartment,
a distinction drawn out in [The models](../03-concepts/models.qmd).

Those trajectories belong to an individual-based malaria transmission model, the lineage
implemented in [`malariasimulation`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/malariasimulation/). That
simulation is slow. A single scenario takes minutes, and a grid of net products crossed with
coverages and resistance levels is a cluster job. `stateMINT` is trained on a large library of
those runs and reproduces their output in milliseconds. A fifty-scenario batch takes under a
second on a laptop CPU. Like any emulator, it is trustworthy only inside the range of settings it
was trained on.

The trained weights are not shipped in the wheel. They live on Hugging Face at
[`dide-ic/stateMINT`](https://huggingface.co/dide-ic/stateMINT), as two checkpoints of about 38 MB
each, one for prevalence and one for cases, and the first call downloads and caches them. Every
later call reads the cache.

## Inputs and outputs

The input is twelve scalars rather than a time series, describing the setting and the campaign,
and the emulator reconstructs the time grid from them. The output is an array of shape `(B, 157)`,
one row per scenario and 157 fortnightly windows spanning day 2190 to day 4374. The campaign lands
at day 3285, which puts three pre-campaign years at the front of every row and three response
years at the back.

Prevalence and cases are separately trained checkpoints, so asking for both means loading both and
calling each once. No single call returns the pair. Please see
[Running Scenarios](../06-scenarios/index.qmd) for a pipeline that loads both and calls each.
